hook: The small, tough leader who opened China's economy to the world.

pages.x: Deng Xiaoping was born in 1904 in Guang'an, in Sichuan. At 16 he went to France on a work and study programme, worked in a car factory and as a kitchen hand, and joined the communists there.
He stood only about 1.5 m tall, and loved playing bridge. In France, it is said, he also came to love croissants.
He marched on the Long March and was a top commander in the civil war. After 1949 he became one of Mao's most powerful officials.

In the Cultural Revolution he was denounced and sent to work in a tractor factory. Red Guards hounded his son, who fell from a window and was left paralysed. He came back, was purged again in 1976, and came back again.

From 1978 he was China's leader. He let farmers sell their crops, opened China to foreign trade and money, and set up special economic zones like Shenzhen, then a small town. "It does not matter if a cat is black or white, as long as it catches mice."
In 1989 students and workers filled Tiananmen Square demanding freedom. Deng backed martial law, and on 4 June troops and tanks cleared the square, killing hundreds, perhaps thousands.
He agreed with Britain that Hong Kong would return to China in 1997 under "one country, two systems". He died months before it did.
Deng's reforms made China the world's second largest economy and lifted hundreds of millions out of poverty, while keeping the Communist Party in total control.
pts: Opened China's economy to the world
Lifted hundreds of millions out of poverty
Ordered the crackdown at Tiananmen Square
